scope: Exact finite-population mathematics and survival-law controls; no neural training or loss implementation
plan_timing: Written before aggregate audit execution; known-answer unit fixtures already passed16 tests. This is not a preregistered independent empirical confirmation.
sample_unit: One hypothetical patient state contains shared bit, four private factors and four slots. Slots are variables within a patient, never independent patients.
distribution: Five independent fair bits: S, two WSI factors, two omic factors; all32 states enumerated. Noise codes add independent or shared encoder randomness, enumerated exactly.
information: Exact entropy/CMI/TC in nats from declared masses, not minibatch MI estimation. Matched marginal reference q(Vk) is a population oracle and is not the neural N0 prior.
rate_identity: sum expected marginal KL = I(A;V_all|G) + TC(V_all|G) - E TC(V_all|A,G) + sum expected marginal-reference mismatch. Factorized posterior removes the negative posterior-TC correction.
survival: Four distinct hazard bins each depend on one private factor and S; independent censor-bin distribution [.1,.1,.1,.7]. Compute event/survival distribution mixtures, never mean hazards.
subset_control: Known-population oracle best one slot per modality; no fitted probe or test-set model selection claim.
additional_controls: Noisy common G=S XOR flip(.25) with constant V versus V=noise correction
XOR task: summed leave-one-out information can double count synergy
Conditioning TC on task can penalize useful XOR
Mask-conditioned decoder can sabotage leave-one-out loss
Gaussian per-slot rate.5 below capacity1 gives no hinge pressure even with copied latent factor
acceptance: Rate identity residual <1e-10; factorwise whole beats oracle one-slot-per-modality; duplicate whole ties one-slot; conditional recoding matches joint content/prediction/rate despite different standalone semantics; local content penalizes cooperative code; correlated encoder noise requires posterior-TC correction.
limits: Privileged synthetic factors and exactly known population only. No clinical semantic identifiability, finite-probe sensitivity or neural optimization claim.
